summary: The TypeScript code compiles without errors and Playwright APIs are used correctly with proper awaiting of all assertions. The test covers the visibility of 26 product cards on the home page, matching the specified test case ID in the title. However, the use of repetitive individual selectors for each product card could be improved for maintainability and reusability. Selectors based on data-test attributes are strong and explicit, reducing flakiness. No asynchronous or API misuse was detected. The absence of more meaningful assertions beyond visibility and lack of navigation or deeper content validations limits assertion strength. The test is straightforward but could be improved by implementing loops, parameterization, or helper methods to avoid redundancy.

issues.description: The test uses repetitive, individual explicit expects for each product card instead of using loops or data-driven methods to iterate through selectors.
issues.recommendation: Use a loop or parameterized test with an array of product IDs to reduce code duplication and improve maintainability.

issues.description: Assertions are limited to visibility checks of product cards and do not verify content, interactivity, or correct product details.
issues.recommendation: Enhance assertions to verify product card contents such as images, titles, or links to improve validation depth.

recommendations: Consider refactoring tests to utilize data-driven approaches for scalability.
Expand assertions beyond visibility to strengthen test reliability and coverage.
Maintain use of explicit data-test attributes as selectors to reduce flakiness.
